title: Upper bound on unit-distance pairs in the plane
statement:
Let $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be $n$ points of the Euclidean plane $\bbr^2$, and consider the unit-distance graph on them, whose edges join the pairs of points lying at distance exactly $1$. Then the number of such edges is at most
\[
\frac{n^{3/2}}{\sqrt{2}} + \frac{n}{4}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: n points in the Euclidean plane R^2
edges = pairs of points at Euclidean distance exactly 1
replaced:
\emph{Given a set of \texttt{n} points in the plane, the number of
pairs of points at distance exactly 1 is at most
\texttt{n\textasciicircum{}\{3/2\}/$\sqrt{}$2 + n/4}.}

$(c)$ Show that, given a set of $n$ points in the plane, the number of pairs of
points at distance exactly 1 is at most $n^{\frac{3}{2}}/\sqrt{2}+n/4$.
